history.summary: Jagdalpur town shrine of Goddess Danteshwari with an official website (maadanteshwarijagdalpur.com, run by 'Temple Estate Jagdalpur', copyright 2017). The site lists idols of Maa Danteshwari, Maa Saraswati and Maa Kali, a Jyot Kalash hall and havan kund, and observes Sharadiya and Chaitra Navratri plus the Dussehra lokotsav with online Jyot Kalash bookings. A local tourism site describes the temple beside the Bastar palace near Gole Bazar as the Bastar royal family's Devi shrine (claims of antiquity there are muddled with the Dantewada temple's history and cannot be verified). DISTINCT FROM the famous 14th-century Danteshwari Shakti Peetha at Dantewada (~80 km southwest at the Shankini-Dhankini confluence). Coordinates from the temple's map listing (19.091529, 82.022158); the geocoder also matched a 'Maa Danteshwari Temple' on Chitrakote Road, Dharmapur (19.09508, 81.9934) — possibly a second Jagdalpur shrine — flagged as unresolved.

name: Maa Danteshwari Mandir, Jagdalpur
town_description: Jagdalpur is the headquarters of Bastar district in southern Chhattisgarh and the region's administrative and cultural centre, gateway to Chitrakote and Tirathgarh waterfalls and home of the 75-day Bastar Dussehra festival.

travel.airport: Maa Danteshwari Airport, Jagdalpur (limited scheduled services); nearest major airport Raipur
travel.road: NH 30 connects Jagdalpur to Raipur and to Dantewada
